key_insight: Uni-XAS turns XAS modeling into a unified cross-modal alignment problem, enabling both spectrum prediction and 3D structure generation from a shared latent space.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a scalable route to learn interpretable structure–property mappings for materials discovery, with potential to accelerate spectral analysis and inverse design.
method: Aligns 1D XAS spectra and 3D atomic structures using XASLip, combining a physics-aware spectral encoder with absorber-aware manifold optimization.
Predicts absolute spectra with retrieval-augmented decoding to reduce energy drift and physical scale collapse.
Generates 3D structures via Permutation-Rectified Flow Matching with type-wise optimal transport to address ligand permutation ambiguity.
evidence_signal: The approach is evaluated on a standardized benchmark of 328,839 structure-spectrum pairs, showing strong results in retrieval, absolute-spectrum prediction, and composition-conditional 3D generation.
watch_item: Inverse structure generation remains intrinsically ill-posed, so performance may depend on benchmark coverage and careful handling of symmetry, composition, and training protocol consistency.
paper_title: Uni-XAS: Alignment-Driven Bidirectional Multimodal Learning for X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy
